title: Why a Gateway: Reducing Coupling and Fan-Out — Check

questions.prompt: What is the primary coupling problem a gateway addresses?
questions.explanation: Direct calls force the client to depend on every service's location and contract; a gateway replaces many dependencies with one stable contract.
options: The frontend must know and depend on the address and contract of every backend service
The backend services run too slowly
The frontend is written in the wrong language
There is no way to log requests

questions.prompt: A healthy gateway is a good place to put rich domain business rules so they are centralized.
questions.explanation: A gateway should stay thin and route/compose. Putting domain logic in it recreates a chokepoint and recentralizes coupling — the 'distributed monolith' anti-pattern.

questions.prompt: When a single screen needs three datasets, what is the gateway's advantage over the browser calling three services?
questions.explanation: Server-side fan-out happens close to the data on internal links, and the browser still issues just one request to the stable public path.
options: It lets the browser cache more aggressively
It can fan out server-side over fast internal links and return one composed response
It removes the need for any backend services
It guarantees the data is always fresh
